title: Monthly earnings and hours changes have different directions across resource and work-limitation cells
source_unit: identified 2025 SIPP person, resource band at month t to direction of valid earnings/hours at month t+1, conditioned on EDISABL

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month-t resource band to month-t+1 direction; work-limiting status = yes

denominator.unit: valid earnings person-month pairs; hours direction uses its own 11,548-pair universe

earnings_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

hours_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

observations.method: Same-person monthly cross-lag from THINCPOV at month t to direction of nonnegative numeric TPEARN and TMWKHRS at month t+1, conditioned on EDISABL=yes; first-month WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Census Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Earnings and hours use separate valid pair universes. Directional estimates are descriptive; a rise or fall does not identify desired hours, job quality, accommodation, or the event causing movement. Approximate intervals are design-based Fay-BRR intervals.
observations.subgroup: Persons reporting a work-limiting condition at month t; estimates retain four resource bands and separate earnings/hours outcome universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher-resource work-limited respondents can show both more earnings increases and more earnings decreases because earnings have more room to move or because job composition differs. Lower-resource hours movement can reflect instability, schedule changes, or opportunity rather than loss or gain in welfare.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month-t resource band to month-t+1 direction; work-limiting status = no

denominator.unit: valid earnings person-month pairs; hours direction uses its own 154,992-pair universe

earnings_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

hours_direction_by_resource_band.unit: percent; direction categories with Fay-BRR standard errors in percentage points, ordered increase/decrease/same

observations.method: Same-person monthly cross-lag and Fay-BRR procedure as the work-limiting observation, conditioned on EDISABL=no.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison retains separate earnings and hours denominators and is not a causal contrast. A person replicate weight does not create a household estimate, and EDISABL is a reported limitation rather than a full health or accommodation measure.
observations.subgroup: Persons not reporting a work-limiting condition at month t; estimates retain four resource bands and separate earnings/hours outcome universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower hours movement does not prove stable or desirable work, and higher earnings movement does not prove improved household room; values can move in either direction and composition differs across cells.

related_sources.claim: The related reproduction audit preserves the base extraction, input fields, pair universes, and Fay-BRR method.

boundary: This is a same-person monthly directional cross-lag, not a causal or household-weighted estimate. EDISABL identifies a reported work-limiting condition, not diagnosis, accommodation, discrimination, or preference. Earnings and hours direction do not establish job quality, care response, recovery, trust, political action, or institutional remedy.
